messages.author: e157d56f92070d6d
messages.subject: Relevant error for rsf.fit
parts:
Hi all,

I am fitting akde-weighted RSFs to some snake telemetry data using rsf.fit. When running the RSF itself I am using the following code including my habitat variables:

RSF <- ctmm:::rsf.fit(ind_data, UD=ud, R=list(Road.surfaces = dist.Road.sur,
                                                Buildings = dist.Build,
                                                Gardens = dist.Pa.Ga,
                                                Scrub = dist.Scru,
                                                Woodland = dist.Wood,
                                                Hedgerows = dist.Hedge,
                                                Pasture = dist.Past,
                                                Meadows = dist.Me.Pa),
                        integrated = TRUE, debias = TRUE, error=0.1)

My question is, for publication standard what is an acceptable level of error? I have been running it with 0.05 (0.1 shown here) but it is very computationally slow.

Thanks for the excellent resource, and any help!

All the best, 

Tom Major

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Relevant error for rsf.fit
parts:
Hi Tom,

If you can put all the rasters into the same gridding (which can't be coarse compared to the home-range scale), then you should just be able to add integrator="Riemann". Then you don't have to worry about the numerical error argument and the computation time is much lower on stationary RSFs.

Otherwise, you could report the relative numerical error threshold of 5%. The default value of 1% would take 25 times longer to run than 5%. So that might also still be an option as something to leave running for a while.

Best,
Chris
